detail.longDescription: I am using Milvus 2.3.3 in standalone mode with PyMilvus 2.3.3 . My collection contains an array field named test , which stores strings. I want to retrieve records where this array contains more than two elements. Filtering by an exact array length works, but using a greater-than comparison produces an error. The array field is defined as follows: from pymilvus import DataType, FieldSchema array_field = FieldSchema( name="test", dtype=DataType.ARRAY, element_type=DataType.VARCHAR, max_capacity=100, max_length=65535, ) With the collection already created and loaded, this query works: collection.query( expr="array_length(test) == 2", output_fields=["test"], ) However, changing the expression to array_length(test) > 2 fails: collection.query( expr="array_length(test) > 2", output_fields=["test"], ) The error is: MilvusException: (code=65535, message=cannot parse expression: array_length(test) > 2, error: GreaterThan is not supported in execution backend) I expected this query to return records whose test array contains three or more elements. The field definition is unchanged, and the equality comparison works on the same collection. Is this a limitation of array_length() in Milvus 2.3.3 , or is there another way to express this filter?
